title: Polynomial-time closure under block XOR search
statement: Let $V$ be a language in $\mathsf{P}$, and let $a,k,a',k'$ be natural numbers. For a binary string $w$, take the first component of its encoded pair as an outer string, then take the first component of that string's encoded pair as $x$; when either parse fails, use the empty string for the corresponding component. Let $y$ be the second component of the outer pair, using the empty string if parsing fails, and set $B=a(|x|+1)^k$ and $N=a'(|x|+1)^{k'}$. The language of strings $w$ for which some $i<N$ has the following property belongs to $\mathsf{P}$: the encoding of the pair $(x, y\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}_\ell u_i)$ is in $V$, where $u_i$ is the length-$B$ block of the second component of the inner pair at position $iB$, truncated at the end, and $\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}_\ell$ denotes bitwise XOR on corresponding positions up to the shorter of the two strings.
